Paddy_Brown_Spot.cause: Nutrient deficient poor soils (low Potassium & Zinc) combined with relative humidity >85% and warm temperatures (25-30Â°C).
symptoms: Small oval to sesame-seed shaped brown spots on leaves with yellow chlorotic halos.
Lesions develop dark brown borders and grayish-white centers as they mature.
In severe cases, leaves wither and turn reddish-brown prematurely.
prevention: Apply balanced Potash (MOP @ 25kg/acre) and Zinc Sulphate (10kg/acre) basal dressing.
Use certified clean disease-free seed; treat seeds with Thiram + Carbendazim @ 2g/kg.
treatment: Organic: Spray Cow Dung Slurry 10% or Neem Seed Kernel Extract (NSKE 5%) twice at 10-day intervals.
Pesticide/Chemical: Spray Mancozeb 75% WP + Carbendazim 12% @ 2g/L water or Propiconazole 25% EC (Tilt) @ 1ml/L.

Paddy_Blast.cause: High relative humidity (>90%), dew, and cool night temperatures (20-25Â°C) with excessive nitrogen fertilization.
symptoms: Eye-shaped or spindle-shaped lesions with reddish-brown borders and gray centers on leaf blades.
Lesions enlarge and coalesce, causing entire leaves to dry up and die.
Neck rot at node bases leading to empty white heads (blank grains).
prevention: Avoid excessive nitrogenous fertilizer application; split N doses.
Treat seeds with Tricyclazole 75% WP @ 2g/kg seed before sowing.
Maintain 5cm water level in field during vegetative stage.
treatment: Organic: Spray 5% Neem oil emulsion or Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 10g/L.
Pesticide/Chemical: Spray Tricyclazole 75% WP @ 0.6g/L or Isoprothiolane 40% EC @ 1.5ml/L water.

Paddy_Sheath_Blight.cause: High humidity (95-100%) and warm temperatures (28-32Â°C), close planting density.
symptoms: Oval or spot-like greenish-gray lesions on leaf sheaths near water level.
Lesions develop dark brown borders with banded appearance.
Lodging of plants and poor grain filling.
prevention: Adopt wider spacing (20cm x 15cm) to improve light penetration.
Remove sclerotia and weeds from field bunds.
treatment: Organic: Soil application of Trichoderma viride @ 2.5 kg/ha mixed with FYM.
Pesticide/Chemical: Spray Hexaconazole 5% EC @ 2ml/L or Validamycin 3% L @ 2ml/L water.

Paddy_Healthy.cause: Balanced irrigation, optimal spacing, and proper micro-nutrient balance.
symptoms: Lush green leaves without spots, lesions, or tip drying.
prevention: Regular field scouting and balanced NPK fertilizer application.
treatment: No treatment required.

Wheat_Stripe_Rust.cause: Cool moist weather (10-15Â°C) with persistent intermittent rains or heavy dew.
symptoms: Bright yellow stripes of rust pustules arranged parallel along leaf veins.
Leaves turn chlorotic, dry prematurely, reducing grain size significantly.
Black teliospores appear on mature leaves late in season.
prevention: Sow certified rust-resistant varieties (e.g., HD 2967, DBW 187).
Avoid late sowing of wheat.
treatment: Organic: Bio-spray of Vermicompost wash (10%) + Bio-agent Bacillus subtilis.
Pesticide/Chemical: Spray Propiconazole 25% EC @ 1ml/L (Tilt) or Tebuconazole 25.9% EC @ 1.5ml/L.

Wheat_Powdery_Mildew.cause: High humidity (80-100%) combined with moderate temperatures (15-22Â°C) and dense foliage.
symptoms: White flour-like powdery patches on upper leaf surfaces and leaf sheaths.
Patches turn dull gray/brown with tiny black fruiting bodies late in season.
Stunted tillering and reduced seed head formation.
prevention: Use balanced seed rate (100 kg/ha) to prevent dense crop canopy.
Avoid excess nitrogen fertilizer.
treatment: Organic: Spray 10% sour buttermilk/whey solution or Wettable Sulphur 80% WP @ 3g/L.
Pesticide/Chemical: Spray Triadimefon 25% WP @ 1g/L or Azoxystrobin 23% SC @ 1ml/L.

Maize_Common_Rust.cause: Cool temperatures (16-25Â°C) with high relative humidity and wind-blown fungal spores.
symptoms: Oval cinnamon-brown pustules scattered across both leaf surfaces.
Pustules rupture releasing powdery rust spores.
Premature leaf senescence in heavy infestations.
prevention: Plant early-maturing hybrid corn varieties.
Rotate corn with non-graminaceous leguminous crops.
treatment: Organic: Neem oil spray 5000 ppm @ 3ml/L water.
Pesticide/Chemical: Spray Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2g/L or Azoxystrobin @ 1ml/L.

Maize_Turcicum_Leaf_Blight.cause: Moderate temperatures (20-28Â°C) accompanied by heavy dew and overcast weather.
symptoms: Long elliptical grayish-green or tan lesions (up to 15cm long) on leaves.
Dark olive-green fungal sporulation visible inside lesions during moist periods.
Blistering and complete burning of leaf canopy.
prevention: Deep plow crop residue immediately after harvest.
Use resistant hybrid varieties.
treatment: Organic: Spray Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 10g/L water.
Pesticide/Chemical: Spray Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5g/L or Propiconazole 25% EC @ 1ml/L.

Tomato_Early_Blight.cause: Warm temperatures (24-29Â°C) with high humidity, heavy rainfall, or overhead irrigation.
symptoms: Dark brown to black spots with distinct concentric rings (target-like pattern) on older leaves.
Yellow halos surrounding leaf lesions leading to premature defoliation.
Sunken, leathery dark lesions on stems and fruit stem end.
prevention: Rotate crops with non-solanaceous crops (e.g., corn, beans) on a 2-3 year cycle.
Use drip irrigation instead of overhead sprayers to keep leaves dry.
Apply organic straw mulch around plant bases.
treatment: Organic: Apply Copper Hydroxide spray @ 2g/L or Bio-fungicide containing Bacillus subtilis.
Pesticide/Chemical: Spray Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2g/L or Chlorothalonil 75% WP @ 2g/L water.

Tomato_Late_Blight.cause: Cool, moist, fog-prone or rainy conditions (15-20Â°C with humidity >90%).
symptoms: Large, dark brown water-soaked lesions expanding rapidly on leaf tips and margins.
White cottony growth on the undersides of leaves under humid conditions.
Dark greasy lesions on stems and firm brown rot on fruit.
prevention: Plant certified disease-resistant tomato varieties.
Space plants adequately (60cm x 45cm) for ventilation.
Avoid planting tomatoes near potatoes.
treatment: Organic: Remove and bury severely infected plants immediately.
Pesticide/Chemical: Spray Metalaxyl 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP (Ridomil Gold) @ 2g/L or Dimethomorph 50% WP @ 1g/L water.

Tomato_Leaf_Curl.cause: Transmitted by Bemisia tabaci (Whitefly) during warm dry spells.
symptoms: Upward curling, puckering, and severe stunting of leaf blades.
Yellowing along leaf margins and bushy stunted plant growth.
Flower abortion and failure to set fruit.
prevention: Install 40-mesh insect-proof net in nurseries.
Set up Yellow Sticky Traps @ 20 traps/acre.
treatment: Organic: Spray Neem oil 10000 ppm @ 3ml/L or NSKE 5% solution.
Pesticide/Chemical: Control vector with Imidacloprid 17.8% SL @ 0.5ml/L or Thiamethoxam 25% WG @ 0.3g/L water.

symptoms: Water-soaked dark green/brown leaf spots turning leaves brittle.
Foul decay odor throughout the field canopy.
Reddish-brown dry rot extending into tuber flesh.
prevention: Hill soil up around plant bases to protect underground tubers from falling spores.
Destroy volunteer potato plants and nightshade weeds near field.
treatment: Organic: Preventive Copper Hydroxide sprays before humid weather.
Pesticide/Chemical: Spray Cymoxanil 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP @ 2g/L or Fenamidone + Mancozeb.

Potato_Blackleg.cause: Infected seed tubers and waterlogged poorly-drained soil.
symptoms: Inky-black slimy decay of the lower stem starting from seed piece.
Yellowing, stunting, and wilting of canopy.
Soft smelly rot inside harvested potato tubers.
prevention: Use certified disease-free seed tubers.
Avoid planting in cold wet waterlogged soils.
treatment: Organic: Dip cut seed tubers in Trichoderma harzianum slurry.
Pesticide/Chemical: Streptocycline 6g per 50L water + Copper Oxychloride 50% WP @ 2.5g/L.

Onion_Purple_Blotch.cause: Warm humid conditions (25-30Â°C) with frequent dew drops.
symptoms: Small water-soaked sunken spots on leaves developing deep purple centers.
Yellow zones extending above and below purple lesions.
Leaves collapse, leading to bulb size reduction.
prevention: Maintain crop rotation of 3 years.
Treat seeds with Thiram or Carbendazim @ 2g/kg.
treatment: Organic: Bio-spray of Trichoderma viride @ 5g/L + Neem formulation.
Pesticide/Chemical: Spray Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5g/L or Tebuconazole 25.9% EC @ 1ml/L.

Pepper_Bacterial_Spot.cause: Warm rainy weather (24-30Â°C) with water splashing.
symptoms: Small water-soaked dark spots on leaves turning brown with chlorotic borders.
Severe defoliation exposing peppers to sunscald.
Raised rough scab-like spots on green fruit.
prevention: Use certified disease-free seed stock.
Avoid overhead irrigation.
treatment: Organic: Fixed copper sprays combined with bio-bactericides.
Pesticide/Chemical: Copper Oxychloride 50% WP @ 2.5g/L + Streptocycline @ 0.1g/L water.

Cotton_Leaf_Curl.cause: Transmitted by Whiteflies (Bemisia tabaci) in warm humid climates.
symptoms: Upward or downward curling of leaf margins.
Thickening of leaf veins and cup-like enations on leaf underside.
Severe plant stunting and drastic boll formation reduction.
prevention: Grow resistant Bt-Cotton hybrids.
Eradicate weed hosts like Abutilon and Xanthium around field.
treatment: Organic: Spray Neem Oil 10000 ppm @ 3ml/L water.
Pesticide/Chemical: Spray Diafenthiuron 50% WP @ 1g/L or Spirotetramat 15.31% OD @ 1ml/L.

Banana_Sigatoka.cause: High rain, high humidity (>80%) and temperatures around 27Â°C.
symptoms: Reddish-brown narrow specks parallel to leaf veins.
Specks enlarge into dark brown/black streaks with gray centers.
Leaves collapse, leading to undersized unripened fruit bunches.
prevention: Ensure good field drainage and prune overcrowded suckers.
Remove heavily infected lower leaves.
treatment: Organic: Mineral oil spray @ 1% mixed with copper fungicide.
Pesticide/Chemical: Propiconazole 25% EC @ 1ml/L or Carbendazim 50% WP @ 1g/L water.

Apple_Scab.cause: Cool wet spring weather with prolonged leaf wetness.
symptoms: Olive-green velvety spots on young leaves turning dark brown.
Deformed, cracked fruit with corky brown scabby patches.
Premature leaf drop in mid-summer.
prevention: Prune orchard trees to open canopy to air and sun.
Rake and destroy fallen leaves in autumn.
treatment: Organic: Apply Liquid Lime Sulfur or Potassium Bicarbonate before rain events.
Pesticide/Chemical: Captan 50% WP @ 2.5g/L or Myclobutanil 10% WP @ 0.4g/L.

Citrus_Canker.cause: Wind-driven rain splashing bacteria onto young flush tissue.
symptoms: Raised corky brown crater-like spots on leaves, stems, and fruits.
Yellow halo surrounding leaf lesions.
Premature fruit drop and twig dieback.
prevention: Plant windbreaks around citrus orchards.
Prune infected twigs during dry winter season.
treatment: Organic: Spray Copper Hydroxide 77% WP @ 2g/L.
Pesticide/Chemical: Copper Oxychloride 50% WP @ 3g/L + Streptocycline 6g per 50L water.

Sugarcane_Red_Rot.cause: High waterlogging, infected seed setts, warm humid monsoon conditions.
symptoms: Third or fourth leaf from top shows yellowing and drying.
Stalk splits open showing reddened internal tissues with white transverse bands.
Alcoholic foul odor from affected canes.
prevention: Select disease-free seed setts from healthy seed nurseries.
Treat setts with hot water (52Â°C for 30 min) or Carbendazim.
treatment: Organic: Soil application of Trichoderma viride @ 5kg/ha.
Pesticide/Chemical: Sett treatment with Carbendazim 50% WP @ 2g/L before planting.

Rice_Blast.cause: High relative humidity (>90%), dew, and cool night temperatures (20-25°C) with excessive nitrogen fertilization.
symptoms: Eye-shaped or spindle-shaped lesions with reddish-brown borders and gray centers on leaf blades.
Lesions enlarge and coalesce, causing entire leaves to dry up and die.

treatment: Organic: Spray 5% Neem oil emulsion or Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 10g/L.
Pesticide/Chemical: Spray Tricyclazole 75% WP @ 0.6g/L water (Beam) or Isoprothiolane 40% EC @ 1.5ml/L.

Rice_Brown_Spot.cause: Nutrient deficient poor soils (low Potassium & Zinc) combined with relative humidity >85% and warm temperatures (25-30°C).
symptoms: Small oval to sesame-seed shaped brown spots on leaves with yellow chlorotic halos.
Lesions develop dark brown borders and grayish-white centers as they mature.
In severe cases, leaves wither and turn reddish-brown prematurely.
prevention: Apply balanced Potash (MOP @ 25kg/acre) and Zinc Sulphate (10kg/acre) basal dressing.

Pesticide/Chemical: Spray Mancozeb 75% WP + Carbendazim 12% @ 2g/L water or Propiconazole 25% EC (Tilt) @ 1ml/L.

Rice_Bacterial_Blight.cause: High humidity (85-100%) and rain storms combined with temperatures of 25-30°C.
symptoms: Water-soaked translucent stripes starting from leaf tips and margins.
Stripes enlarge, turning wavy yellow to straw-colored withered margins.
Milky bacterial ooze droplets on young leaves in early morning.
prevention: Grow resistant varieties (e.g. Improved Samba Mahsuri).
Avoid clip-topping seedling leaves at transplanting.
treatment: Organic: Spray Fresh Cow Dung Slurry 20% + Neem Cake 5% extract.
Pesticide/Chemical: Spray Streptocycline 6g + Copper Oxychloride 50% WP @ 500g in 200L water per acre.

Rice_Healthy.cause: Balanced irrigation, optimal spacing, and proper micro-nutrient balance.
symptoms: Lush green leaves without spots, lesions, or tip drying.
prevention: Regular field scouting and balanced NPK fertilizer application.
treatment: No treatment required.
